text:
maria.g: Hey team, running into AccessDenied when attempting to kms:Decrypt the envelope key after an sts:AssumeRole into the vault account. CLI call fails with:

maria.g: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cek.bin --encryption-context FileId=abc123
Error: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/ro-cross/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222333444555:key/abcd-ef01

ajay.k: Can you paste the CloudTrail event for Decrypt? and the KMS key policy (redact ARNs if necessary). Also confirm whether you're using a session policy when assuming the role.

maria.g: CloudTrail event (trimmed):
{
  "eventName": "Decrypt",
  "errorCode": "AccessDenied",
  "userIdentity": {
    "type": "AssumedRole",
    "arn": "arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/ro-cross/session-2026-03-18",
    "sessionIssuer": { "arn": "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ro-cross" }
  },
  "requestParameters": { "encryptionContext": { "FileId": "abc123" } }
}

maria.g: Key policy (redacted):
```json
{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowAccountRootUsage",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222333444555:root" },
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowKeyUseForService",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/vault-service" },
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

ajay.k: A couple of things to note: the effective principal on the Decrypt call is the assumed-role ARN (sts::assumed-role/RoleName/session). KMS key policies need to grant that principal (or the role itself) permission. Your key policy only grants the account root and a vault-service role in the key account. It doesn't grant the cross-account role (arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ro-cross).

ajay.k: Also check for an AssumeRole session policy. If you passed a session policy when assuming the role (Policy param), it can further restrict permissions. Example session policy that would block decrypt: 
```json
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{"Effect":"Deny","Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"*"}] }
```

leo.ops: Another gotcha: if you're using grants (CreateGrant) from the key account, those are short-lived and require you to pass the grantToken on the decrypt call. CloudTrail will show CreateGrant events if that's the case. Also check encryption context mismatch — KMS will deny if the encryption context provided at Decrypt doesn't match the one used at Encrypt.

maria.g: We didn't create a grant. We're doing envelope encryption: data key created in account 222..., ciphertext stored in S3 in account 111... We then assume ro-cross in account 222... to decrypt the wrapped key. No session policy was passed.

ajay.k: In that flow the simplest fix is to add the ro-cross role ARN to the key policy in account 222333444555 and explicitly allow kms:Decrypt (and kms:GenerateDataKey if needed) for that role. Example snippet to add to key policy principals: 
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ro-cross" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

leo.ops: If you prefer not to modify the key policy, create a grant in the key account where GranteePrincipal is the role ARN and then include the returned grantToken in the Decrypt call. Grants are useful for transient cross-account access without changing the key policy.

security-bot: CloudTrail link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/home?region=us-west-2#/events?EventId=EXAMPLE (sanitized). Detected multiple AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt this morning, correlated with assume-role sessions.

maria.g: Quick test — added the role ARN to key policy (temporary change) and retried:

maria.g: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cek.bin --encryption-context FileId=abc123
DecryptedKey: (binary output)

maria.g: Confirmed fixed after key policy change.

ajay.k: Great. Follow-ups: 1) revert temporary wide grants and harden to only allow the specific role ARN, 2) add a comment in the key policy with ticket ID, 3) if this is going to be a recurring pattern, either standardize on cross-account grants or document the key policy template in the security playbook.

leo.ops: For audit, annotate the CloudTrail events with ticket number and add a Console-only CloudWatch alarm for repeated kms:AccessDenied spikes so we catch permission regressions early.

maria.g: Thanks — will make a PR to add the role to the key policy template and open a follow-up to evaluate grants vs key-policy. :thumbsup:
